strategy: static-musl eligible binaries inside a relocatable Nix closure launched by yzx-envelope
justification: LifeOS uses the flexnetosMuslToolchain for the eligible Rust and launcher binaries so the shipped executable surface is static-pie and does not require a host dynamic loader. The complete runtime is not honestly reducible to one static file: PostgreSQL/RuVector, WebKitGTK, bwrap, and the Nushell yzx-envelope engine have distinct host or closure ownership. Therefore the release combines static-musl artifacts with a relocatable extracted closure, binds that closure at /nix through yzx-envelope, and reports every remaining non-musl dependency and fallback. This is the smallest strategy that preserves the PostgreSQL/RuVector authority boundary while proving the portable execution surface from the moved bundle.

options_considered.verdict: rejected as the sole release format
options_considered.trade_offs: Nix bundle preserves dependency closure fidelity and is easy to reproduce, but it does not by itself establish a clean-prefix launch contract or hide the host store. It also leaves the native PostgreSQL/RuVector and desktop dependency boundary implicit unless the launcher and receipt classify each dependency explicitly.

Static musl produces small, host-loader-independent binaries and is directly reproducible with flexnetosMuslToolchain. It cannot cover WebKitGTK, PostgreSQL/RuVector, bwrap, or other dynamically loaded platform surfaces, so using it alone would make a false full-stack portability claim.

A relocatable extracted closure retains the exact Nix runtime needed by yzx-envelope and the native support tools, and the moved-prefix test proves the host store is hidden. It is larger than a single static binary and still requires explicit classification of host-owned PostgreSQL/RuVector and desktop integrations.

nix-user-chroot would provide a familiar closure entry point, but the live host has kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns enabled and the required unprofiled userns path is denied. The resulting userns failure is not an acceptable portable release mechanism; yzx-envelope records the same policy boundary and uses the profiled bwrap fallback.

steps: Build eligible Rust and launcher binaries with flexnetosMuslToolchain and record file type and SHA-256.
Classify PostgreSQL/RuVector, WebKitGTK, bwrap, and every other non-musl dependency with an owner and fallback.
Extract the Nix closure into the bundle's nixroot and verify closure paths are complete.
Launch the moved prefix through yzx-envelope with the extracted closure bound at /nix.
Run a store-hidden relocation test and a static musl workload with an empty /nix surface.
Retain the measured receipt and block stronger portability claims when host-Nix dependence remains.
